context: …nal folk medicine, dried earthworm (地竜) was used as a fever reducer. The expression 蚯蚓に小便を【かけると】腫れる is a folk superstition warning children not to urinate on earthworms.
note: The marked word is a combination of the verb 'かける' and the particle 'と'.

context: 豆をぽりぽり食べるのが【やめられない】。
english: I can't stop munching on beans.
note: The marked word is an inflected form of 'yameru' combined with the potential negative suffix '-rareru'.

context: 【やり】 (giving) + 取り (receiving) - the back-and-forth of giving and receiving
note: The marked word is 'やり', a noun form of 'yaru', not the verb 'yaru' itself.

context: 七五三のとき、娘に初めて草履を履かせたら、歩き【にくそうだった】。
english: When I had my daughter wear zori for the first time at her Shichi-Go-San celebration, she seemed to have trouble walking.
word: にくい + そうだ + った
note: The marked word is an inflected form of 'にくい' combined with 'そう' (seeming) and the past tense 'だった'.

context: - 【やっ】ちゃった: I did it (made a mistake)
note: The marked word is an inflected form of やる, but the entry is for the base form. The marked word is part of the construction やっちゃった, which is a contraction of やってしまった.

context: 審査員が点数を【つける】。
note: This 'tsukeru' means 'to give/assign (scores)', which is a different kanji and sense from the entry's 'to turn on, to attach'.
